original_question: Does every Banach space X of density greater than the continuum c have an infinite unconditional basic sequence? If not in full generality, does adding hypotheses such as reflexivity change the answer?
target_in_paper: Problem 20 in Section 13, “Unconditional basic sequences in non-separable spaces.”
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper’s intended question: it asks about Banach spaces of density strictly above the continuum, it asks for an infinite unconditional basic sequence, and it asks whether adding a structural hypothesis such as reflexivity could change the answer. That is very close to the official formulation in Section 13.
missing_details: The continuum should be written as the cardinal 𝔠, not as the Banach space c; in Banach-space notation this distinction matters.
“Density” should be stated as density character.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether every Banach space with density character > 𝔠 has the stated property.
“Infinite unconditional basic sequence” should be understood as a countably infinite basic sequence that is unconditional.
The paper phrases the second clause as whether additional properties, such as reflexivity, make a difference; reflexivity is the named example, not a replacement of the main problem.

The nearby context should be kept in mind: the paper records a counterexample at density 𝔠 (Theorem 21) and also a reflexive counterexample in the adjacent discussion (Theorem 22), so the official open problem is deliberately asked only above 𝔠.
The paper does not add further restrictions such as separable dual, special basis length beyond countable infinity, or a distinguished scalar field in the statement.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space of density character strictly greater than the cardinality of the continuum 𝔠. Must X contain a countably infinite unconditional basic sequence? More generally, can the answer change under additional structural hypotheses on X, for example if X is assumed to be reflexive?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 20 in Section 13 rather than an earlier part of the paper. In the Introduction, the paper lists “Unconditional basic sequences in non-separable spaces” as one of its main topics, and Section 13 then states the corresponding open problem in essentially the same form as your draft. The nearby theorems explain why both parts of the question belong together: Theorem 21 gives a negative example at density 𝔠, Theorem 22 shows that reflexivity does not trivialize the issue, and Theorem 23 gives a consistency result in the positive direction at a larger density. So the sharp paper-faithful version is the large-density question above 𝔠 together with the explicit follow-up about whether extra assumptions such as reflexivity affect the answer.
